the volatile anesthtetic isofluranes, halothane and enflurane prolong the time course of inhibitory synaptic transmission in cultured rat hippocampus neurons by increasing the amplitude and duration of the slower component of the inhibitory postsynpatic currents (IPSC) and by decreasing the amplitude and duration the faster component.
volatile anesthetics increase the duration of GABAA receptor-mediated synaptic currents in cultured rat neurons by prolonging the decay phase of the synaptic current.
volatile anesthetics prolong the duration of inhibitory postsnaptic currents (IPCs) in cultured rat hippocamal neurons.

the effects of anesthetics on synaptic transmission in the central nervous system.
the effects of anesthetic agents on the kinetics of the GABA receptor/channel complex.
the effects of volatile anesthetic agents on the kinetics of the GABA-mediated inhibitory synaptic current.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

these volatile anesthetics prolong the time course of inhibitory synaptic currents by altering the kinetics of the GABA(A) receptor/channel complex, and that this action is consistent with the known physiological effects that accompany the use of volatile anesthetiocs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
volatile anesthetics prolong synaptic inhibition in the central nervous system (CNS) and that this prolongation may be due to a direct action on GABA receptors in the brain.
volatile anesthetics increase the amplitude of the slow component of the GABA-mediated IPSC, decrease the amplitude of the fast component, and increase the overall duration of the GABAergic IPSC.

anesthetic agents prolong the decay time of GABAergic synaptic currents.
